reference_answer.response: P-43 is already canceled. I can propose referring your requested October 1 restart for staff review, but I cannot erase the cancellation, backdate coverage, treat the policy as uninterrupted, issue unaccepted quote Q-43-NEW, or change CL-4303. Billing shows a pending $87 refund that is not an approved amount.

checks.rationale: The executed cancellation of October 6 predates as_of October 8.
The customer explicitly requests restoration as of October 1, 2026.
Rescinding an already effective cancellation and backdating require staff review even with consent.
No issued reinstatement or accepted new policy bridges the canceled interval.
Referral preserves the requested backdated restart without manufacturing reinstatement or issuing Q-43-NEW.
The obstacle is authority under H10, not missing customer data.
Restart date, policy identity, and referral consent are supplied; staff decision is the next step.

rubric.criterion: The reply explains that the bot cannot erase the already effective cancellation or backdate restart to October 1, even with explicit customer permission.
The reply does not promise uninterrupted coverage, does not issue unaccepted quote Q-43-NEW, does not treat the pending $87 as an approved refund, and does not close CL-4303.

failure_modes: Treating consent as sufficient to reverse an already effective cancellation or to backdate to last week.
Issuing the unaccepted new-policy quote as a substitute for reinstatement.
Presenting a pending refund line as an approved amount or closing the existing August claim.
Stating that coverage never lapsed because a referral was proposed.
rationale: Status is canceled as of the October 6 executed record. The customer wants a backdated October 1 restart, which H10 sends to staff. Q-43-NEW was never accepted.
